title: Lecture 3 — logic levels, CMOS gates, and power
summary: Truth tables define what a gate does; voltage ranges make those bits electrically reliable; complementary pMOS and nMOS networks implement the gates; and switching activity, voltage, capacitance, frequency, and leakage determine their power use.
body:
Begin with the behavioural layer: a truth table lists every input combination and the resulting output. The electrical layer then replaces ideal bits with guaranteed voltage ranges and noise margins. At transistor level, pMOS devices form a pull-up network to $V_{\mathrm{DD}}$ and nMOS devices form a pull-down network to ground; complementary series and parallel arrangements implement NOT, NAND, and NOR.

CMOS power has two components:

$$\begin{aligned} P_{\mathrm{dynamic}} &= \frac{1}{2} C \left(V_{\mathrm{DD}}\right)^2 f \\ P_{\mathrm{static}} &= I_{\mathrm{leak}} V_{\mathrm{DD}} \end{aligned}$$
